main_chase_cards.name: _____'s Pikachu
main_chase_cards.why: This is the Natta Wake finale turning the player into part of the card. The blank name line is not decoration; it is the object asking for a human owner, a birthday, and a story, which makes it one of the cleanest bridges between manga, play, and collection memory.

key_artists.name: Kagemaru Himeno
examples: How I Became a Pokemon Card manga
key_artists.why: Himeno is load-bearing twice here: she created the manga volume and illustrated this birthday-card reprint. The final book turns her gentle comic premise into a player-facing card that literally leaves a blank for the collector.

claims.text: The local unnumbered-promo catalog records September 23, 2001 as the source-row release date for the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6 _____'s Pikachu insert.

Bulbapedia's volume page records the first-edition book publication as September 22, 2001 with ISBN 4840104026, so the catalog preserves a one-day book/publication versus promo-row boundary rather than forcing a false single date.
Bulbapedia identifies Volume 6 as the sixth and final How I Became a Pokemon Card manga volume, created by Kagemaru Himeno, with _____'s Pikachu as the included promo card.
The final chapter list includes Akari and Pikachu's Birthday, which gives the birthday-card promo a direct story-context hook inside the volume.
The card page credits Kagemaru Himeno as illustrator for the How I Became a Pokemon Card unnumbered promotional print, while the volume page identifies Himeno as the manga creator.

The _____'s Pikachu page places the Natta Wake print in a broader lineage: the original Japanese calendar card, English Wizards/Pikachu World routes, the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6 reprint with different artwork by the same artist, and later 25th Anniversary reprints.

The collector point is not simply that this is a Pikachu promo. It is a player-identity object: the Japanese name asks the owner to write a name, the Pokedex data includes a birthdate line, and the attack only becomes special on the player's birthday.

For high-stakes matching, the Natta Wake Vol. 6 print must be separated from the 1998 All Card Calendar Japanese print, English Wizards Black Star Promo 24, Pikachu World Collection 2000, Celebrations Classic Collection, and Japanese Promo Card Pack 25th Anniversary Edition versions.

narrative.human_title: How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6: the book that ends by handing Pikachu back to the reader
narrative.why_it_matters: Vol. 6 is the sentimental close of the Natta Wake lane. After five book promos about Pokemon becoming cards, the last one centers Pikachu, Birthday Surprise / おたんじょうび, and a blank owner line. It is a perfect little assembly object: Himeno's manga, Himeno's card art, a child writing a name, a rule that cannot survive tournament seriousness, and a collector market that has to keep several visually adjacent birthday Pikachu routes apart.

special_identification_instructions.title: How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6 route boundary
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller note, or agent memory says _____'s Pikachu, _____のピカチュウ, Happy Birthday Pikachu, Natta Wake Birthday Pikachu, How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6, ポケモンカードになったワケ 6, Kagemaru Himeno, ISBN 4840104026, or source index 245.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Use this route packet when an agent needs to decide whether a claim is specifically the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6 book-insert route rather than another Birthday Pikachu route.
steps: Anchor the claim to How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6 / ポケモンカードになったワケ 6, not merely to any Happy Birthday Pikachu or Wizards Promo 24 listing.
Preserve the local promo-row date of September 23, 2001 while noting Bulbapedia's September 22, 2001 first-edition book publication date as a date-boundary, not a contradiction to hide.
Require the single modeled local source index 245 when the agent is matching this catalog route.
Check that the described card is _____'s Pikachu / _____のピカチュウ, not a generic Pikachu, birthday-themed sticker, or later anniversary card.
Confirm the Kagemaru Himeno creator-illustrator loop when using the manga route as context.
Use Akari and Pikachu's Birthday as story context only; do not treat chapter context as proof that a seller's physical card came from a particular book.
Keep the route separate from Vol. 1 Mankey, Vol. 2 Psyduck, Vol. 3 Jynx, Vol. 4 Sunkern, and Vol. 5 Hoppip.
Do not infer sealed-book completeness from the loose-card route. A book, dust jacket, obi, insert, or card state must each be evidenced separately.
Do not infer market value from the Natta Wake route; route identity and price require separate evidence.
If the buyer specifically wants the Vol. 6 insert, require a front/back image or trusted catalog witness that distinguishes the artwork and border details from the 1998 calendar and later versions.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors _____'s Pikachu as source index 245 in the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6 unnumbered-promo source row.

Bulbapedia identifies the card as _____'s Pikachu / _____のピカチュウ, translated as Write your name here's Pikachu, a Lightning Basic Pokemon card with HP 50, LV.17, No. 25, Fighting weakness, and retreat cost 1.
Bulbapedia credits Kagemaru Himeno as illustrator for the How I Became a Pokemon Card unnumbered promotional print.
The card's attack is Birthday Surprise / おたんじょうび for Lightning Lightning, doing 30+ damage, with the extra-damage condition tied to whether it is the player's birthday.

Bulbapedia notes that Wizards immediately banned the card on release because any player could claim it was their birthday, and that both Japanese prints carry a clause to the right of the illustrator name saying the card cannot be used at official tournaments.

The Natta Wake print is one member of a larger Birthday Pikachu lineage that includes the 1998 Japanese All Card Calendar original, English Wizards/Pikachu World routes, the Vol. 6 manga reprint with different artwork by the same artist, and 25th Anniversary versions.
The why of this card is the blank. It converts the player from owner into printed subject, which is exactly why it is charming for binders and impossible for clean tournament policy.

Agents should treat the Natta Wake Vol. 6 print as a version-specific route, not as interchangeable with Wizards Promo 24, the 1998 calendar print, Pikachu World Collection, Celebrations, or other birthday Pikachu cards.

narrative.human_title: _____'s Pikachu: the card where the collector enters the text box
narrative.why_it_matters: Birthday Pikachu is one of those cards that explains why Pokemon cards became social objects. The Vol. 6 version is not only a Pikachu promo; it is a Himeno-drawn book-card that asks for a name, a birthday, and a little suspension of tournament seriousness. It belongs in the catalog as an identity trap and as a tiny essay on why kids loved these objects enough to write themselves into them.

special_identification_instructions.title: Natta Wake _____'s Pikachu source-index-245 checks
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, scan, want, seller note, or agent memory says _____'s Pikachu, _____のピカチュウ, _____ no Pikachu, Happy Birthday Pikachu, Natta Wake Birthday Pikachu, Kagemaru Himeno, Birthday Surprise, おたんじょうび, LV.17, HP 50, No. 25, or source index 245.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Use this card packet when an agent needs to separate the Natta Wake Vol. 6 _____'s Pikachu from the calendar, Wizards, Pikachu World, Celebrations, or generic Birthday Pikachu routes.
steps: Start with the exact name: _____'s Pikachu / _____のピカチュウ / _____ no Pikachu. Do not collapse it into generic Pikachu.
Require the blank-owner framing in the name line. This is the identity core of the card, not optional flavor.
Check the Natta Wake / How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 6 route when the buyer asks for the book insert specifically.
Verify Kagemaru Himeno / 姫野かげまる as the illustrator for the How I Became a Pokemon Card unnumbered promotional print before using the artist route.
Check that the card profile matches the source: LV.17, HP 50, No. 25, Lightning Basic, Fighting weakness, retreat cost 1.
Check for Birthday Surprise / おたんじょうび as the attack and the birthday-dependent 30+ damage concept.
Look for the Japanese official-tournament-use clause near the illustrator area when distinguishing Japanese prints; absence or mismatch should trigger a version check, not an automatic fake claim.

Separate this card from the 1998 Japanese All Card Calendar print, English Wizards Black Star Promo 24, Pikachu World Collection 2000, Celebrations Classic Collection, and Promo Card Pack 25th Anniversary Edition versions.
If the seller claims a book-origin copy, ask for seller-controlled evidence of the card and, separately, any book/insert provenance they want counted. Do not infer one from the other.
If a listing says Happy Birthday Pikachu without naming Natta Wake or Vol. 6, treat it as underspecified until artwork, language, border text, and route evidence are supplied.

Keep price, popularity, and later reprint fame separate from the catalog identity. The protocol can make the route legible; it cannot make the physical card spendable without seller evidence and gate authority.
